slot.brief: Simple related-rates problem, e.g. rate of increase of a circle's area given the rate of radius increase; differentiate A = πr².

stem: The radius of a sphere is increasing at $2$ cm min$^{-1}$. At the instant when its radius is $3$ cm, how fast is its volume increasing?
working:
$V=\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$\n$\dfrac{dV}{dt}=4\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt}=4\pi(3)^2(2)=72\pi$ cm$^3$ min$^{-1}$.

Independent check: $V=\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$, so $\frac{dV}{dt}=4\pi r^2\frac{dr}{dt}=4\pi(3)^2(2)=72\pi\ \text{cm}^3\text{min}^{-1}$.
